checks: The actual caps are fixed, regular, nonvertical, and have positive aggregate coarea. Multiplying a response weight by its S_l gives its geometric weight up to normalization. Positive scaling preserves the support and minimality. A positive rescaling of a cap equation changes S_l and u_l reciprocally, leaving g_l unchanged.

The compact nonempty T has an extreme maximizer for each fixed vertex. Independence of the supported (1,g_l) columns follows by signed perturbation. Its g-column kernel contains the positive feasible vector and has dimension one, because any other independent kernel vector could be made zero-sum by subtracting a multiple of the positive vector. Thus the support is a single minimal circuit with at most d+1 members.

The equality-constraint dual has free scalar t and free v, with t+v dot g_l>=h_X,l. Taking the smallest t gives the stated max with a minus sign. As a rational calibration, take u=(2,-1), S=(1/2,3/2), and h=(1,0). The balanced response weights are (3/5,2/5); multiplying by S balances the u normals. At v=2/5 both dual affine terms equal 3/5, matching the primal.

The contact and hinge lemmas apply to each actual exposed lifted vertex and the chosen response profile. Its constructed potential has positive denominator and at least the strict-incidence objective. The finite nonempty vertex list then gives an actual maximizing certificate, without exchanging an infinite supremum and an infimum.
